subject: FinSight API — latency backlog causing elevated p95/p99
messages:
From: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@finsighthealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: sarah.li@finsighthealth.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden spike in API tail latency — urgent

Marissa,

We started seeing user-facing slowdowns this morning around 07:00 PT across our integration. P95 jumped from ~600ms to ~2.8s and p99 climbed above 6s. Throughput reports show request retries and a backlog on your hosted endpoint (redwood-model:rlhf-2-large). This is causing timeouts in our ingestion pipeline and a visible regression in our web app.

Can you confirm whether this is on Redwood's side or ours? We are in production and this is impacting clinical users. We need a short bridge and an ETA for mitigation.

Attached: sample request IDs and a short snippet of our logs.

—Tom
Tom Hayes
Head of Integrations, FinSight Health
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@finsighthealth.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 08:33:42 -0800
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in API tail latency — urgent

Tom — thanks for the heads up and the sample IDs, really appreciate that. We’re pulling traces now. I’ve looped in Dylan (runtime on-call) and Laura from CS who is your account lead.

Immediate plan:
- Dylan will collect a traces + queue-depth snapshot and confirm if batching/queue depth or kernel contention is causing the backlog.
- We’ll provision a short-term routing change to move FinSight traffic to a higher-throughput shard if safe.
- We’ll share a diagnostic bundle and a mitigation ETA within 30 minutes.

Can you confirm if you were on a long-streaming generation yesterday evening or if there were any large-batch inference jobs kicked off from your side? That helps scope whether this is head-of-line blocking from very long requests.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@finsighthealth.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 08:47:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in API tail latency — urgent

Tom / Marissa — I’m live on this. Initial findings (08:45 PT):
- Host-level traces show queue_depth on the endpoint spiking to ~750 concurrent pending requests (our target SLO is <200 for this tier).
- Continuous batching appears to have aggregated many small requests, but we also see several very large token-generation requests (>=2k tokens) that are holding KV-cache resources and inflight slots.
- Kernel-level stalls on the GPU were correlated with high variance sequences; p99 jumps when the scheduler can't evict a blocking request.
- Autoscaler did not spin up extra capacity because the request pattern exceeds our burst threshold for the current shard (burst_policy: off for this customer until committed capacity).

Immediate mitigations applied (08:50 PT):
- Forced a temporary routing change to a sibling shard with spare capacity for FinSight (routing change id: route-20270115-01).
- Increased per-client concurrency cap from 32 -> 48 for your API key as a temporary relief.
- Disabled continuous batching for this shard to avoid head-of-line batching delays and applied lightweight prefix caching where safe.

I’ve attached a trace bundle (redwood-traces-20270115.zip) and a short CSV of sampled request latencies. Please let us know if you see improvement on your side; I’ll continue to monitor logs and queue_depth.

—Dylan (runtime on-call)
From: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@finsighthealth.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Li <sarah.li@finsighthealth.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 09:02:10 -0800
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in API tail latency — urgent

Thanks Dylan — we can confirm latency dropped within ~6 minutes of your routing change. P95 back to ~700ms and p99 down to ~1.8s for the short window. That said, the spike recurred at 09:20 PT and we observed a second backlog. Attached new logs (finsight_request_logs_01-15.csv).

We did run a few long-batch exports overnight (batch export of anonymized transcripts, ~1.8k tokens avg) — apologies, we scheduled those from our side to run at 02:00 PT but they were meant to be throttled. We need guidance on best practices for large offline exports so this doesn't affect the real-time path.

Tom
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@finsighthealth.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 09:36:58 -0800
Subject: Re: FinSight API — latency backlog causing elevated p95/p99

Tom — thanks for the quick confirmation and the logs. We have two tracks here: short-term mitigations and a medium-term action plan.

Short-term (today):
- Maintain the routing to the higher-capacity shard for the next 2 hours while Dylan keeps queue_depth under surveillance.
- If you can re-schedule or throttle your overnight exports, please do so; we can help you identify an export window that’s safe for your traffic tier.

Medium-term (by end of next week):
- We recommend a split of traffic: real-time routes pinned to a lower-concurrency, low-latency shard; offline exports routed to a dedicated batch endpoint (we can provision a Dedicated pool or a scheduled burst window).
- Engineering will propose a configuration: per-key concurrency caps, batch-size limits, and an automated fallback that rejects large token-generation requests on the real-time route with a clear 429 + Retry-After.

We’ll create a short MAP (mutual action plan) and a proposal for dedicated export capacity. I’ve uploaded a one-pager and the MAP draft here: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/CS/FinSight/MAP_plan.xlsx

Cc’ing Sean for executive visibility on potential credits and SLA exceptions while we investigate root cause and deliver safeguards.

—Laura
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@finsighthealth.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 15:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinSight API — latency backlog causing elevated p95/p99

Tom — I’m Sean (Head of Sales Ops). I wanted to make sure you have executive attention while we finalize actions. Appreciate your patience and the clear logs.

We’ll do the following immediately:
- No-charge credits for the impacted window and a one-time expedited provisioning of a dedicated batch endpoint for your exports (trial Dedicated pool for 7 days).
- Our Engineering team will deliver a hardened routing policy to reject oversized real-time generation requests with explicit guidance and client-side SDK guards.
- We’ll run a joint runbook review in the next 48 hours to validate autoscaler thresholds, burst policies, and per-key concurrency defaults so this pattern doesn’t repeat.

I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the runbook review and the MAP sign-off. Thanks again for working with us through this — we’ll close the loop and share a root-cause summary once the team completes the postmortem.

—Sean
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
